📋 1. Executive Summary & Data Pipeline Architecture

Core Research Problem & Objective

Patients incur heavy out-of-pocket costs due to brand-name prescribing, where chemically identical medicines sell at radically disparate prices. This project builds a transparent data science framework to match exact generic alternatives, measure manufacturer pricing premiums, and compute actionable prescription savings.

الملخص التنفيذي بالعربية (Executive Highlights)
يوفر المشروع محركاً ذكياً لفهرسة 21,714 دواء وتحديد البدائل المتكافئة كيميائياً بدقة (نفس المادة الفعالة + الشكل الصيدلاني + التركيز الموحد). أثبت التحليل أن 79.8% من الأدوية تُباع بأسعار تفوق البديل الأرخص، مع وسيط توفير يبلغ 28.6%، وتوفير يفوق 50% لـ 15.4% من الأدوية.

1.1 Data Engineering & Entity Normalization

The source dataset was cleaned and structured into a 3NF relational database (data/medicine.db), establishing complete referential integrity with zero orphan records:

Entity / SQL Table Record Count Primary Key Data Pipeline Status
medicines 21,714 brand_id Extracted unit prices, pack sizes, and normalized strengths
generics 1,711 generic_id Active chemical pharmaceutical substances (100% Unique INN)
manufacturers 240 manufacturer_id Licensed pharmaceutical manufacturing companies
drug_classes 421 drug_class_id Deduplicated from 453 raw rows into 421 unique canonical classes
indications 2,043 indication_id Therapeutic clinical indications and use cases
dosage_forms 113 dosage_form_id Standardized formulations (Tablets, Capsules, Injections, Syrups)

1.2 Regex Price Extraction Engineering

  • Price Coverage: Unit price was extracted from complex packaging strings, recovering 20,357 valid prices (93.75% coverage).
  • Integrity Rule: 1,279 ambiguous entries with competing multi-pack prices were deliberately preserved as NULL to prevent false calculations.
  • Integrity Checks: Zero primary key duplicates, zero foreign key orphans, and zero negative prices across the entire database.

📊 2. Market Structure & Price Distribution Dynamics

Empirical evaluation of the 20,357 priced products reveals heavy skewness and significant portfolio concentration among top industrial producers:

Figure 1: Logarithmic distribution of unit prices. Median = 15.05 BDT; Mean = 349.99 BDT.
Figure 2: Top 10 pharmaceutical manufacturing companies by total marketed products.

2.1 Key Structural Market Findings

  • 23-Fold Price Skewness: While the arithmetic mean price is 349.99 BDT, the median price is only 15.05 BDT. High-cost oncology biologics and immunosuppressants (reaching up to 175,000 BDT) heavily distort the average, making median metrics essential for public health analysis.
  • 75% Mass Market Threshold: Three-quarters of all marketed medicines cost below 50 BDT per unit, confirming that routine outpatient care revolves around low-cost essential compounds.
  • Industrial Portfolio Concentration: The top 15 manufacturers produce 48% of all commercial medicines. Market volume is led by Square (1,180 brands), Incepta (995 brands), Beximco (840 brands), Renata (720 brands), and Eskayef (685 brands).
Strategic Takeaway: Routine healthcare revolves around a compact set of high-volume generic molecules produced by major domestic conglomerates, creating a prime opportunity for generic substitution.

🧬 3. Chemical Equivalence Engine & Price Dispersions

To eliminate arbitrary comparisons, our engine identifies true clinical alternatives using an exact 3-tuple matching rule:

Exact Chemical Equivalence Matching Rule
GenericName(A) = GenericName(B)  •  DosageForm(A) = DosageForm(B)  •  NormalizedStrength(A) = NormalizedStrength(B)

🏭 4. Manufacturer Price Index (MPI) Benchmarking

To benchmark company pricing strategies objectively, we formulated the Manufacturer Price Index (MPI), normalizing each product against its exact formulation group median:

Price Index = Brand Price / Equivalent Group Median Price   |   MPI = Median(Price Index) for company (sample ≥ 30)
Figure 4: Manufacturer Price Index (Top 6 Budget vs. Top 6 Premium Companies).

4.2 Key Pricing Power Insights

  • Market Anchors: Market leaders (Square, Incepta, Beximco) anchor the market median at exactly 1.00x.
  • Budget Producers: Local budget firms (Gonoshasthaya, Delta) offer products 20% to 24% below median prices.
  • Premium Importers: Multinationals (Novartis, Radiant, Sandoz) charge a 17% to 63% brand premium over identical alternatives.

Clinical Distinction: A therapeutic drug class groups compounds by pharmacological mechanism. Different compounds within a class (e.g. Omeprazole vs. Esomeprazole) are not automatically interchangeable without clinical review. Our equivalence engine matches only identical active molecules.

💰 6. Patient Savings Economics & Clinical Case Studies

Across 18,476 comparable medicines, 14,745 brands (79.81%) are priced higher than the category minimum, unlocking substantial patient savings:

Figure 6: Share of non-cheapest brands (79.8%) and savings tier distribution.

6.1 Savings Distribution Highlights

  • Median Savings: 28.6% per prescription switch.
  • Mean Savings: 30.5% per prescription switch.
  • Extreme Overpricing (≥ 50% Savings): 15.42% of brands (2,849 medicines) cost more than double the cheapest equivalent.
  • 20% to 40% Tier: 42.1% of all non-cheapest brands fall into the standard 20% to 40% savings bracket.

7.2 Clinical Limitations & Policy Recommendations

⚠️ Medical & Regulatory Disclosures:
• Chemical equivalence (≥ identical generic, form, strength) does not substitute for laboratory bioequivalence (BE) certification.
• Designed for economic transparency; patients must consult licensed clinicians before altering prescriptions.

Strategic Action Items:

  • Mandate Generic Prescribing: Require clinicians to write active chemical names on prescriptions.
  • Target Rational Price Caps: Introduce Maximum Retail Price (MRP) limits on molecules with spreads > 3.0x.
  • Public Transparency: Deploy digital pricing portals to empower consumers against arbitrary markups.
